items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I was good friends with Ellis Burton, who was the owner of the Yellow Front Cafe

ctx.x: You were talking about when Count Basie was in Kansas City...

Well, we get to Kansas City...Kansas City to me at that point was the highlight. It wasn't the climax, but just the highlight...well, I don't guess it was the highlight, but it was such an exciting city, where that...at six o'clock you 'O have Julia Lee, George Lee, Andy Kirk, Mary Lou Williams, Hot Lips Page, Willie Mack Washington who was the first drummer with Bennie Moten, Jo Jones...well, I don't think Jo was around in the beginning. And then you'd have Dan Miner and Budd Johnson and Keg Johnson, Booker…

This was fascinating to me. And then I was...I called myself half-slick, you know what I mean. I was good friends with Ellis Burton, who was the owner of the Yellow Front Cafe, and Piney Brown...(unintelligible).. Piney Brown and--Big Piney had gone to Chicago to live, but Little Piney was there--and Felix Payne, who was another patron of jazz musicians. And Big Joe Turner, Jimmy Rushing. And this to me was just so fascinating and amazing, that I just couldn't...I couldn't really get it in my mind that here I am,…
